name: Science
blurb: Biology, chemistry, physics, and earth science compressed into the concepts UPCAT repeats, with a checkpoint exam after each group.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take a short mixed-science diagnostic covering biology, chemistry, physics, and earth science. Clear this node to open the first group of topics.
nodes.tip: Sort every miss by branch, then start with the branch that has the most misses.

nodes.title: Scientific Method & Measurement
nodes.description: Hypotheses, variables, controlled experiments, and SI units with significant figures.
nodes.tip: For any experiment question, identify the independent variable first — it anchors everything else.

nodes.title: Cell Structure & Function
nodes.description: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, organelles, membranes, and transport.
nodes.tip: Link each organelle to a factory job; function questions outnumber structure questions.

nodes.title: Matter & Its Properties
nodes.description: States of matter, physical vs chemical changes, mixtures, and separation techniques.
nodes.tip: Classify first: if a new substance forms, the change is chemical.

nodes.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Table
nodes.description: Subatomic particles, electron configuration, and periodic trends.
nodes.tip: Trends follow position: radius grows down and left; electronegativity grows up and right.

nodes.title: Forces & Equilibrium
nodes.description: Types of forces, free-body diagrams, friction, and balanced vs unbalanced systems.
nodes.tip: Draw the free-body diagram before choosing an equation; never skip the normal force.

nodes.title: Motion & Newton's Laws
nodes.description: Kinematics graphs, acceleration, and Newton's three laws applied to real systems.
nodes.tip: In a velocity–time graph, slope is acceleration and area under the line is displacement.

nodes.title: Earth's Structure & Rocks
nodes.description: Layers of the Earth, the rock cycle, minerals, and soil formation.
nodes.tip: Sketch the rock cycle once from memory; most items test transitions, not definitions.

nodes.title: Plate Tectonics & Earthquakes
nodes.description: Plate boundaries, fault types, seismic waves, and volcanoes.
nodes.tip: Divergent → ridge, convergent → trench or mountain, transform → fault. Match boundary to landform.

nodes.title: Scientific Foundations Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering the scientific method, cells, matter, atomic structure, forces, motion, Earth structure, and plate tectonics.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the next group.

questions.prompt: A student tests how fertilizer affects plant growth. What is the independent variable?
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one the experimenter deliberately changes, which is the amount of fertilizer.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is the main site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into proteins. Mitochondria release energy, and the nucleus stores genetic material.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting produces a new substance, iron oxide. The other examples change form or appearance without creating a new substance.

questions.prompt: The atomic number of an element equals its number of what?
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined by the number of protons in the nucleus. Protons plus neutrons give the mass number.

questions.prompt: Newton's first law is also known as the law of what?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law says an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a net force acts on it. This property is inertia.

nodes.title: Lab Safety & Data
nodes.description: Safe handling of glassware and chemicals, lab equipment, and recording measurements accurately.
nodes.tip: Read the meniscus at eye level and record units with every measurement.

nodes.title: Genetics & Heredity
nodes.description: DNA, Mendelian crosses, Punnett squares, and pedigree analysis.
nodes.tip: For dihybrid crosses, split the problem into two monohybrid crosses and multiply.

nodes.title: Human Body Systems
nodes.description: Circulation, respiration, digestion, excretion, and nervous coordination.
nodes.tip: Trace one oxygen molecule and one glucose molecule through the body; most items follow those paths.

nodes.title: Chemical Bonding
nodes.description: Ionic vs covalent bonds, Lewis structures, and intermolecular forces.
nodes.tip: Metal + nonmetal is ionic; nonmetal + nonmetal is covalent. That one rule answers many items.

nodes.title: Reactions & Stoichiometry
nodes.description: Balancing equations, reaction types, moles, and limiting reactants.
nodes.tip: Balance oxygen and hydrogen last; leave the most complex formula for the final count.

nodes.title: Work, Energy & Momentum
nodes.description: Work, power, conservation of energy, and collisions.
nodes.tip: Check whether the system is closed; if it is, mechanical energy at the start equals the end.

nodes.title: Waves, Light & Sound
nodes.description: Wave properties, reflection and refraction, sound, and the electromagnetic spectrum.
nodes.tip: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength. Rearrange that one equation for most wave items.

nodes.title: Weather, Climate & Oceans
nodes.description: Atmosphere layers, fronts, storms, ocean currents, and climate patterns.
nodes.tip: Low pressure means rising air and rain; high pressure means sinking air and fair weather.

nodes.title: Solar System & the Universe
nodes.description: Planets, seasons, tides, stars, and the Big Bang.
nodes.tip: Seasons come from axial tilt, not distance from the Sun — a classic UPCAT trap.

nodes.title: Matter & Systems Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering lab data, genetics, body systems, bonding, reactions, energy, waves, weather, and space.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the advanced group.

questions.prompt: A student measures a mass three times and gets 9.8 g, 9.9 g, and 10.0 g. These repeated measurements best demonstrate what?
questions.explanation: Precision describes how close repeated measurements are to each other. Accuracy describes how close they are to the true value.

questions.prompt: In a cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa × Aa), what is the probability of an offspring showing the recessive trait?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives AA, Aa, Aa, and aa. Only aa shows the recessive trait, so the probability is 1/4 or 25%.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins return blood to the heart.

questions.prompt: An ionic bond usually forms between which two types of elements?
questions.explanation: Ionic bonds form when a metal transfers electrons to a nonmetal. Two nonmetals typically form covalent bonds.

questions.prompt: A wave has a frequency of 4 Hz and a wavelength of 3 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength = 4 Hz × 3 m = 12 m/s.

nodes.title: Data Analysis & Graphs
nodes.description: Choose the right graph, read trends, identify outliers, and distinguish correlation from causation.
nodes.tip: A line graph shows change over time; a bar graph compares categories. Match the graph to the question.

nodes.title: Ecology & Populations
nodes.description: Food webs, population dynamics, carrying capacity, and energy flow through ecosystems.
nodes.tip: Removing a top predator cascades downward; trace the chain two steps before answering.

nodes.title: Evolution & Classification
nodes.description: Natural selection, evidence for evolution, speciation, and the major classification groups.
nodes.tip: Natural selection acts on heritable variation that already exists in a population.

nodes.title: Acids, Bases & Solutions
nodes.description: pH, neutralisation, salts, concentration, and the behaviour of solutions.
nodes.tip: pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, and above 7 is basic. Each whole step is a tenfold change.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry Basics
nodes.description: Carbon bonding, hydrocarbons, functional groups, and common organic reactions.
nodes.tip: Carbon forms four bonds. Count them first when checking whether a structure is valid.

nodes.title: Heat & Thermodynamics
nodes.description: Heat transfer, specific heat, phase changes, and the laws of thermodynamics.
nodes.tip: During a phase change the temperature stays constant even though heat is still being added.

nodes.title: Electricity & Magnetism
nodes.description: Circuits, Ohm's law, series vs parallel, and the link between electricity and magnetism.
nodes.tip: For circuits, find total resistance first, then total current, then branch values.

nodes.title: Climate Change & Cycles
nodes.description: The greenhouse effect, carbon and water cycles, climate evidence, and human impact.
nodes.tip: Distinguish weather (short-term) from climate (long-term patterns); many items hinge on that difference.

nodes.title: Natural Resources & Pollution
nodes.description: Renewable and nonrenewable resources, conservation, and types of pollution.
nodes.tip: Renewable does not mean unlimited; a resource can renew slowly and still be overused.

nodes.title: Advanced Science Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering data analysis, ecology, evolution, acids and bases, organic chemistry, thermodynamics, electricity, climate, and resources.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the final simulation.

questions.prompt: In a food web, removing a top predator most likely causes what?
questions.explanation: Without the predator, fewer prey are eaten, so the prey population can grow. The effect then cascades through the rest of the food web.

questions.prompt: Natural selection acts directly on what?
choices: Traits acquired during an individual's lifetime
questions.explanation: Natural selection favours heritable traits that improve survival and reproduction. Acquired traits are not passed on genetically.

questions.prompt: A solution has a pH of 3. How should it be classified?
questions.explanation: pH values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral, and values above 7 are basic.

questions.prompt: Organic compounds are built around which element?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-based compounds. Carbon's four bonds allow large, varied molecules.

questions.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected to a 3 Ω resistor. What current flows?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V ÷ R = 12 V ÷ 3 Ω = 4 A.

nodes.title: Science Simulation
nodes.description: Mixed science sets under time pressure with error-log review.
nodes.tip: Log every miss by topic; revisit the weakest branch before the next simulation.
